title: Thiriet by TDS wins Estoril as Greaves takes the LMP2 title
dek: Nicolas Lapierre led Thiriet by TDS to victory in the Estoril 4 Hours, but Greaves finished second from the back of the LMP2 grid to take the title from pole-sitting Jota.

chapters.title: Three crews, one title
text: The 4 Hours of Estoril on 18 October 2015 closed the European Le Mans Series season with the LMP2 crown still unsettled. Jota Sport arrived with a single-point lead over Greaves Motorsport, the two Gibson 015S-Nissan crews separated on the road by almost nothing. Greaves held the tie-break on wins, two to Jota’s one, and Thiriet by TDS Racing sat ten points behind the leaders with one victory of its own. The French Oreca 05 realistically needed to win and hope both Gibsons hit trouble; a fourth place or better for the Gibsons would be enough to keep it out.

The entry was ten cars, and the French team had made the biggest change. Nicolas Lapierre replaced Tristan Gommendy alongside Pierre Thiriet and Ludovic Badey, the team hoping the former factory driver’s knowledge of the identical Oreca 05 run elsewhere would unlock pace it had not found all year. AF Racing arrived on Dunlops with its two BR01s, quick at Le Castellet and expected to be more reliable, while Krohn Racing had added Olivier Pla to its Ligier-Judd line-up. Murphy Prototypes, Eurasia, Algarve Pro and Pegasus completed the field.

The weather made the weekend unpredictable. Free practice on Saturday morning was red-flagged 26 minutes early because of rising wind and heavy rain, and the afternoon session was extended to two hours to compensate. On a damp, drying track Jon Lancaster’s 1:32.346 in the Greaves Gibson led the second session, with Lapierre second and Mikhail Aleshin third in the AF Racing car. Harry Tincknell kept the Jota car fourth.

chapters.title: Albuquerque takes the point
text: Qualifying began on a wet track that dried unevenly, which left the Michelin and Dunlop runners swapping fortunes. Léo Roussel put the Pegasus Morgan-Nissan on top for much of the session and, with the track still soaked, Olivier Pla and the Krohn Ligier climbed to second before the leading Dunlop runners switched to intermediates. Lapierre moved up as well, fastest of the Dunlop cars in the Thiriet by TDS Oreca, and Aleshin found grip in the AF Racing BR01.

Lancaster briefly went top in the Greaves Gibson, beating Pla by one thousandth of a second. Then Filipe Albuquerque, driving at his home circuit, lowered the benchmark to 1:43.510 just before yellow flags ended any chance of an improvement, and Jota took pole and the extra championship point. That stretched its lead over Greaves to two points. Pla’s 1:44.319 was second on the grid in the Krohn Ligier, ahead of Lapierre on 1:45.018, Aleshin on 1:45.207 and Roussel on 1:45.281.

Greaves did not benefit from its qualifying effort: the car started from the back of the ten-car LMP2 grid, tenth, with Bjorn Wirdheim at the wheel. Behind the title fighters Nico Pieter de Bruijn took sixth in the Eurasia Oreca 03R, Andrea Roda seventh for Algarve Pro, Nathanaël Berthon eighth for Murphy and Nicolas Minassian ninth in the second AF Racing car.

chapters.title: Spins at the start, Albuquerque pulls away
text: The race got under way at 1pm. Wirdheim, starting from the back, found himself in the middle of early chaos as Tracy Krohn, Roussel and James Winslow all spun in the opening laps. He avoided them and was soon in a good position, but the title battle was otherwise shaped at the front, where Albuquerque went straight into one of his long-distance charges from pole.

The Jota car stretched its advantage through the first stint, and for a time the top three in the championship held the top three places on the road: Jota, Greaves and Thiriet by TDS. The Pegasus Morgan was out of contention early, so the lead group quickly narrowed to the three title contenders and the two AF Racing BR01s.

chapters.title: The downpour reshuffles the title fight
text: The balance shifted at the first round of stops. The AF Racing crew in the #21 chose not to take tyres, jumped ahead of the Jota car and led through the middle stages with Mikhail Aleshin and Kirill Ladygin sharing the work. A sudden downpour in the second hour then turned a drying track into a skating rink in seconds. Simon Dolan spun the Jota Gibson into a gravel trap, lost the lead and with it any realistic chance of the title, eventually dropping to a lap down in the process.

Greaves moved to the front on the road as Gary Hirsch worked his way up from the back of the grid, and the lead fight settled into a three-way contest between Hirsch, the #21 and Pierre Thiriet. More showers kept making the choice of tyre difficult, and the AF Racing crew was punished for staying on intermediates as the track dried again. The Murphy Oreca #48, which had briefly run in the top three on pace in Michael Lyons’ hands, stopped for good after half distance, while the Eurasia #33 kept going at its own pace, eventually finishing two laps down.

chapters.title: Lapierre breaks clear, Greaves holds on
text: Lapierre took the Oreca for the run to the flag and set about reeling in Ladygin, who was still on intermediates on a drying track, passing him quickly. By the start of the last hour the Thiriet by TDS Oreca was about 53 seconds clear of Lancaster in the Greaves Gibson, with the #21 on slicks and the second AF Racing car close behind. Tincknell was now charging hard in the Jota, gradually shrinking the gap to Lancaster.

With 40 minutes left the margin between the two Gibsons was around 33 seconds, and both team managers had been called to race control. Lancaster was handed a stop and go penalty for a pit-lane infringement with about 20 minutes to run. He served it immediately, but crucially stayed ahead on the road, with Aleshin in the AF Racing car still in the way of the Jota. The Jota then looked unable to push, and the title fight was effectively decided there.

chapters.title: A second win for Thiriet by TDS
text: Lapierre brought the Oreca home to win the 4 Hours of Estoril, sharing the victory with Thiriet and Badey after 137 laps. It was the team’s second win of the season. Lancaster took the flag second on the same lap, enough to give Greaves the team title and its three drivers, Hirsch, Wirdheim and Lancaster, the LMP2 drivers’ crown. Aleshin completed the podium for AF Racing, also on the lead lap, after an additional stop for tyres had cost the Russian crew a possible victory.

Jota finished fourth, a lap down, after a day when the car’s title chances slipped away in the gravel and then on pace. Tincknell set the fastest lap of the race, a 1:33.077, but it could not repair the damage. The second AF Racing car was fifth on 136 laps, Eurasia sixth two laps down, then Algarve Pro and Krohn seven and eight, both six laps behind the winner. Murphy’s #48 and the Pegasus #29 were not classified.

chapters.title: Greaves crowned, Jota third
text: Thiriet by TDS finished the championship second, which pushed Jota down to third. The victory at Estoril was the French team’s second of the year, and Lapierre’s late-season arrival in the car had turned a team that was short of pace into the day’s winner. It was not quite enough: it had needed both Gibsons off the podium, and Greaves held on to second.

For Greaves the result brought the LMP2 teams’ title, while Hirsch, Wirdheim and Lancaster took the drivers’ crown. Hirsch, who also won the LMPC title in 2013, added the overall LMP2 drivers’ title, and both Wirdheim, who had come close in Super GT, and Lancaster won their first sportscar championships. Tincknell explained afterwards that something on the rear wing had broken, costing him a lot of time in his closing stint. AF Racing’s Aleshin had been in the mix for the win until the tyre choice and the extra stop undid the effort.

The champions were celebrated at the awards night at the Centro de Congressos in Estoril. Sam Hignett of Jota was named Man of the Year, the award citing the team’s contribution to the spectacle of the season and its double programme for 2016 in partnership with Arden Racing.

The ACO used the weekend to announce the Michelin GT3 Le Mans Cup for 2016, a six-round series on ELMS weekends, and said prize money would be offered to successful ELMS teams from next season, with the amounts not yet decided. The 2016 Prologue test at Paul Ricard was moved to 22-23 March, which will be the series’ next outing.

facts.t: Pole and a point for Jota
facts.v: Filipe Albuquerque took pole with 1:43.510 on a drying Estoril track, earning the extra point that put Jota two points clear of Greaves.
